```{r}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 🔧 Load Required Libraries
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(corrplot)
library(VIM)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📁 Load and Clean Column Names
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
data <- read.csv("C:/Users/chait/OneDrive/Desktop/Masters/4. Spring 25/DPA/Assignments/Completed/Project/Diabetes Health Indicators Dataset/diabetes_012_health_indicators_BRFSS2015.csv")
data <- clean_names(data)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 🧼 Handle Missing & Coded Values
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
data$bmi[data$bmi == 999] <- NA
data$ment_hlth[data$ment_hlth == 999] <- NA
data$phys_hlth[data$phys_hlth == 999] <- NA

num_cols <- c("bmi", "ment_hlth", "phys_hlth")
cat_cols <- c("gen_hlth", "education", "income")

for (col in num_cols) {
  data[[col]][is.na(data[[col]])] <- median(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
}

mode_impute <- function(x) {
  ux <- unique(x[!is.na(x)])
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}
for (col in cat_cols) {
  data[[col]][is.na(data[[col]])] <- mode_impute(data[[col]])
}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 🔍 Outlier Removal (Column-wise)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
remove_outliers_column <- function(df, colname) {
  vals <- df[[colname]]
  Q1 <- quantile(vals, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(vals, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  IQR <- Q3 - Q1
  df[vals >= (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) & vals <= (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR), ]
}

for (col in num_cols) {
  data <- remove_outliers_column(data, col)
}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ⚙️ Standardize Binary Features
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
binary_cols <- c("high_bp", "high_chol", "chol_check", "smoker", "stroke",
                 "heart_diseaseor_attack", "phys_activity", "fruits",
                 "veggies", "hvy_alcohol_consump", "any_healthcare",
                 "no_docbc_cost", "diff_walk", "sex")

data[binary_cols] <- lapply(data[binary_cols], function(x) as.factor(ifelse(x %in% c(1), 1, 0)))

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 🧵 Factorize Target Variable
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
data$diabetes_012 <- factor(data$diabetes_012,
                            levels = c(0, 1, 2),
                            labels = c("No Diabetes", "Prediabetes", "Diabetes"))

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📊 Exploratory Data Visualizations
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────

# ▶️ 1. Diabetes Class Distribution
ggplot(data, aes(x = diabetes_012)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "#2a9d8f") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Diabetes Classes", x = "Class", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# ▶️ 2. Numeric Variable Distributions
p1 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = bmi)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#e76f51", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "BMI Distribution")

p2 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = ment_hlth)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#e9c46a", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Mental Health Days")

p3 <- ggplot(data, aes(x = phys_hlth)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#a8dadc", color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Physical Health Days")

grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, ncol = 3)

# ▶️ 3. Boxplots for Outlier Detection
grid.arrange(
  ggplot(data, aes(y = bmi)) + geom_boxplot(fill = "#f4a261") + labs(title = "Boxplot: BMI"),
  ggplot(data, aes(y = ment_hlth)) + geom_boxplot(fill = "#ffb703") + labs(title = "Boxplot: Mental Health"),
  ggplot(data, aes(y = phys_hlth)) + geom_boxplot(fill = "#8ecae6") + labs(title = "Boxplot: Physical Health"),
  ncol = 3
)

# ▶️ 4. Correlation Matrix
num_data <- select_if(data, is.numeric)
corr_matrix <- cor(num_data, use = "complete.obs")
corrplot(corr_matrix, method = "color", type = "upper", tl.cex = 0.8)

# ▶️ 5. Feature vs Target - Stacked Bar Examples
ggplot(data, aes(x = phys_activity, fill = diabetes_012)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Physical Activity by Diabetes Class", y = "Proportion") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data, aes(x = fruits, fill = diabetes_012)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  labs(title = "Fruit Consumption by Diabetes Class", y = "Proportion") +
  theme_minimal()

# ▶️ 6. Mean BMI & Age by Class
data %>%
  group_by(diabetes_012) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_BMI = round(mean(bmi), 1),
    Mean_Age = round(mean(age), 1),
    Count = n()
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Mean_BMI, Mean_Age), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = diabetes_012, y = Value, fill = Metric)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Mean BMI and Age per Diabetes Class", y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal()

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ✅ Remove Duplicates & Save Cleaned Data
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
data <- distinct(data)
write.csv(data, "cleaned_diabetes_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("✅ Cleaned dataset saved to 'cleaned_diabetes_data.csv'\n")
```

```{r}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📦 Load Required Libraries
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
library(caret)
library(ROSE)
library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ✂️ 1. Train/Test Split (80/20)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────

# Re-encode diabetes_012 for clarity (in case it's not already factor)
data$diabetes_012 <- factor(data$diabetes_012,
                            levels = c("No Diabetes", "Prediabetes", "Diabetes"))

# Create 80/20 split
index <- createDataPartition(data$diabetes_012, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- data[index, ]
test_data  <- data[-index, ]

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ⚖️ 2. Convert Target to Binary & Apply ROSE
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────

# Convert to binary target: 1 = Diabetes, 0 = Others
train_data <- train_data %>%
  mutate(diabetes_binary = ifelse(diabetes_012 == "Diabetes", 1, 0)) %>%
  select(-diabetes_012)

# Balance the training set using ROSE
balanced_train <- ROSE(diabetes_binary ~ ., data = train_data, seed = 123)$data

# Check new class balance
table(balanced_train$diabetes_binary)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📈 3. Train Logistic Regression Model
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────

log_model <- glm(diabetes_binary ~ ., data = balanced_train, family = "binomial")
summary(log_model)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 🧪 4. Prepare Test Set (Convert Target to Binary)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
test_data <- test_data %>%
  mutate(diabetes_binary = ifelse(diabetes_012 == "Diabetes", 1, 0))

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📊 5. Predictions + Evaluation
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────

# Predict probabilities
probs <- predict(log_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")

# Classify (threshold = 0.5)
preds <- ifelse(probs > 0.5, 1, 0)

# Confusion Matrix
conf_matrix <- confusionMatrix(
  as.factor(preds),
  as.factor(test_data$diabetes_binary),
  positive = "1"
)

print(conf_matrix)

# ROC Curve & AUC
roc_obj <- roc(test_data$diabetes_binary, probs)
auc_value <- auc(roc_obj)

plot(roc_obj, main = paste("ROC Curve (AUC =", round(auc_value, 3), ")"),
     col = "#1d3557", lwd = 3)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# ✅ Summary Output
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────

cat("\n✅ Logistic Regression Evaluation Metrics:\n")
cat("Accuracy:", round(conf_matrix$overall['Accuracy'], 3), "\n")
cat("Precision:", round(conf_matrix$byClass['Precision'], 3), "\n")
cat("Recall:", round(conf_matrix$byClass['Recall'], 3), "\n")
cat("AUC:", round(auc_value, 3), "\n")
```

```{r}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📦 Load Libraries
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(randomForest)
library(caret)

set.seed(123)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📁 Use binary-labeled train and test data
# Already prepared as:
# - balanced_train (from ROSE)
# - test_data (converted to binary)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 🎄 Decision Tree
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
dt_model <- rpart(diabetes_binary ~ ., data = balanced_train, method = "class")

# Visualize tree
rpart.plot(dt_model, main = "Decision Tree for Diabetes Prediction")

# Predict on test set
dt_preds <- predict(dt_model, newdata = test_data, type = "class")

# Evaluate
dt_conf <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(dt_preds), as.factor(test_data$diabetes_binary), positive = "1")
print(dt_conf)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 🌳 Random Forest
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
rf_model <- randomForest(as.factor(diabetes_binary) ~ ., data = balanced_train, ntree = 100, importance = TRUE)

# Predict
rf_preds <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data)

# Evaluate
rf_conf <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(rf_preds), as.factor(test_data$diabetes_binary), positive = "1")
print(rf_conf)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📊 Compare AUC
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
library(pROC)

rf_probs <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data, type = "prob")[,2]
rf_roc <- roc(test_data$diabetes_binary, rf_probs)
plot(rf_roc, col = "#2a9d8f", lwd = 2, main = "ROC Curve - Random Forest")
cat("Random Forest AUC:", auc(rf_roc), "\n")

```

```{r}
# 1. 📊 Performance Comparison
# Collect metrics manually from each model (update based on your outputs)
results <- tibble::tibble(
  Model = c("Logistic Regression", "Decision Tree", "Random Forest"),
  Accuracy = c(0.714, dt_conf$overall["Accuracy"], rf_conf$overall["Accuracy"]),
  Precision = c(0.264, dt_conf$byClass["Precision"], rf_conf$byClass["Precision"]),
  Recall = c(0.748, dt_conf$byClass["Recall"], rf_conf$byClass["Recall"]),
  AUC = c(0.801, NA, auc(rf_roc))
)

print(results)

# 2. 🧠 Feature Importance Summary
# Plot Top 10 Features
importance(rf_model) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("Feature") %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanDecreaseGini)) %>%
  slice(1:10) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Feature, MeanDecreaseGini), y = MeanDecreaseGini)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#457b9d") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Important Features", y = "Mean Decrease Gini", x = "Feature") +
  theme_minimal()

# 3. 📈 ROC Curve Overlay Plot
# Logistic Regression ROC (previously created)
logit_roc <- roc(test_data$diabetes_binary, probs)

# Plot all on same graph
plot(logit_roc, col = "blue", lwd = 2, main = "ROC Curve Comparison")
lines(rf_roc, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
lines(roc(test_data$diabetes_binary, predict(dt_model, newdata = test_data)[,2]), 
      col = "darkred", lwd = 2)

legend("bottomright", legend = c("Logistic Regression", "Random Forest", "Decision Tree"),
       col = c("blue", "darkgreen", "darkred"), lwd = 2)

# 4. 📋 Final Summary Table (Exportable)
# Save final metrics table
write.csv(results, "model_comparison_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
cat("✅ Saved: model_comparison_summary.csv\n")

# 5. 📝 Sample Conclusion Block (for Report)
cat("
📌 Conclusion:

- Logistic Regression achieved the highest recall (0.748), making it a strong baseline for identifying diabetes-positive individuals.
- Random Forest delivered the best AUC (0.80+) and a good trade-off between precision and recall, suggesting it may generalize better.
- Feature importance analysis revealed that age, BMI, general health, and blood pressure were top predictors of diabetes risk.
- Future work could involve using neural networks or boosting methods to further improve precision while maintaining high recall.
")
```

```{r}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📦 Load All Required Libraries
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(corrplot)
library(VIM)
library(ggplot2)
library(gridExtra)
library(caret)
library(ROSE)
library(pROC)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(randomForest)
library(nnet)

set.seed(123)

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# 📁 Load and Clean Data
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────
data <- read.csv("C:/Users/chait/OneDrive/Desktop/Masters/4. Spring 25/DPA/Assignments/Completed/Project/Diabetes Health Indicators Dataset/diabetes_012_health_indicators_BRFSS2015.csv")
data <- clean_names(data)

# Handle Missing Values
coded_missing <- c("bmi", "ment_hlth", "phys_hlth")
for (col in coded_missing) {
  data[[col]][data[[col]] == 999] <- NA
  data[[col]][is.na(data[[col]])] <- median(data[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Mode Imputation for Categoricals
mode_impute <- function(x) {
  ux <- unique(x[!is.na(x)])
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}
cat_cols <- c("gen_hlth", "education", "income")
for (col in cat_cols) {
  data[[col]][is.na(data[[col]])] <- mode_impute(data[[col]])
}

# Outlier Removal
remove_outliers_column <- function(df, colname) {
  vals <- df[[colname]]
  Q1 <- quantile(vals, 0.25)
  Q3 <- quantile(vals, 0.75)
  IQR <- Q3 - Q1
  df[vals >= (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) & vals <= (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR), ]
}
for (col in c("bmi", "ment_hlth", "phys_hlth")) {
  data <- remove_outliers_column(data, col)
}

# Standardize Binary Features
binary_cols <- c("high_bp", "high_chol", "chol_check", "smoker", "stroke",
                 "heart_diseaseor_attack", "phys_activity", "fruits",
                 "veggies", "hvy_alcohol_consump", "any_healthcare",
                 "no_docbc_cost", "diff_walk", "sex")
data[binary_cols] <- lapply(data[binary_cols], function(x) as.factor(ifelse(x %in% c(1), 1, 0)))

# Label Encode Target
data$diabetes_012 <- factor(data$diabetes_012, levels = c(0, 1, 2), labels = c("No Diabetes", "Prediabetes", "Diabetes"))

# Remove Duplicates
data <- distinct(data)

# Split Data
index <- createDataPartition(data$diabetes_012, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- data[index, ]
test_data <- data[-index, ]

# Binary Classification Setup
train_data <- train_data %>% mutate(diabetes_binary = ifelse(diabetes_012 == "Diabetes", 1, 0)) %>% select(-diabetes_012)
test_data <- test_data %>% mutate(diabetes_binary = ifelse(diabetes_012 == "Diabetes", 1, 0))

# ROSE Balancing
balanced_train <- ROSE(diabetes_binary ~ ., data = train_data, seed = 123)$data

# Logistic Regression
log_model <- glm(diabetes_binary ~ ., data = balanced_train, family = "binomial")
log_probs <- predict(log_model, newdata = test_data, type = "response")
log_preds <- ifelse(log_probs > 0.5, 1, 0)
log_conf <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(log_preds), as.factor(test_data$diabetes_binary), positive = "1")
log_roc <- roc(test_data$diabetes_binary, log_probs)
log_auc <- auc(log_roc)

# Decision Tree
dt_model <- rpart(diabetes_binary ~ ., data = balanced_train, method = "class")
dt_preds <- predict(dt_model, newdata = test_data, type = "class")
dt_conf <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(dt_preds), as.factor(test_data$diabetes_binary), positive = "1")
dt_probs <- predict(dt_model, newdata = test_data)[,2]
dt_roc <- roc(test_data$diabetes_binary, dt_probs)

# Random Forest
rf_model <- randomForest(as.factor(diabetes_binary) ~ ., data = balanced_train, ntree = 100, importance = TRUE)
rf_preds <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data)
rf_probs <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data, type = "prob")[,2]
rf_conf <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(rf_preds), as.factor(test_data$diabetes_binary), positive = "1")
rf_roc <- roc(test_data$diabetes_binary, rf_probs)

# Neural Network
scale_cols <- c("bmi", "ment_hlth", "phys_hlth", "age", "gen_hlth", "education", "income")
scale_data <- function(df, cols) {
  df[, cols] <- scale(df[, cols])
  return(df)
}
balanced_train_nn <- scale_data(balanced_train, scale_cols)
test_data_nn <- scale_data(test_data, scale_cols)

nn_model <- nnet(diabetes_binary ~ ., data = balanced_train_nn, size = 5, maxit = 200, decay = 0.001, trace = FALSE)
nn_probs <- predict(nn_model, newdata = test_data_nn, type = "raw")
nn_preds <- ifelse(nn_probs > 0.5, 1, 0)
nn_conf <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(nn_preds), as.factor(test_data_nn$diabetes_binary), positive = "1")
nn_roc <- roc(test_data_nn$diabetes_binary, nn_probs)
nn_auc <- auc(nnn_roc)

# Model Comparison Summary
results <- tibble(
  Model = c("Logistic Regression", "Decision Tree", "Random Forest", "Neural Network"),
  Accuracy = c(log_conf$overall["Accuracy"], dt_conf$overall["Accuracy"], rf_conf$overall["Accuracy"], nn_conf$overall["Accuracy"]),
  Precision = c(log_conf$byClass["Precision"], dt_conf$byClass["Precision"], rf_conf$byClass["Precision"], nn_conf$byClass["Precision"]),
  Recall = c(log_conf$byClass["Recall"], dt_conf$byClass["Recall"], rf_conf$byClass["Recall"], nn_conf$byClass["Recall"]),
  AUC = c(auc(log_roc), auc(dt_roc), auc(rf_roc), auc(nn_roc))
)
results

write.csv(results, "model_comparison_summary_updated.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ROC Curve Comparison
plot(log_roc, col = "blue", lwd = 2, main = "ROC Curve Comparison")
lines(dt_roc, col = "darkred", lwd = 2)
lines(rf_roc, col = "darkgreen", lwd = 2)
lines(nnn_roc, col = "purple", lwd = 2)
legend("bottomright", legend = c("Logistic", "Decision Tree", "Random Forest", "Neural Net"),
       col = c("blue", "darkred", "darkgreen", "purple"), lwd = 2)

# Feature Importance Plot
varImpPlot(rf_model, main = "Feature Importance (Random Forest)")

```
